model_annotation: The graph displays the accuracy (ACC) in percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1 to 1000, while the y-axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 40% to 44%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at around 44% and increases to about 56%. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) begins at roughly 40% and rises to about 47%. The MEMIT method (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at approximately 43% and increases to around 55%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) shows the highest accuracy, starting at about 51% and increasing to over 65%. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
